resolution: Raised the localstore value ceiling so a detailed imported model is never store-bound. Verified the whole value path is heap-backed end to end (v8 binding argToStringAlloc allocates the exact UTF-8 length; the write-queue WriteJob owns a heap []u8 freed by the writer thread; SQLite bindText handles up to ~1GB), so MAX_VALUE was only a sanity guard. Bumped it 4MB->64MB in framework/storage/localstore.zig — a high-poly Studio model (its EditMesh JSON rides in the editor-state value) no longer trips BufferTooSmall, while a genuinely runaway multi-hundred-MB value is still caught. With the store no longer the limiter, lifted MAX_IMPORT_TRIS 25k->150k in importMesh.ts (the cap now reflects editor responsiveness, since every face is a JS object the Studio edits/paints/undoes) and raised the dialog's GRID_MAX 200->512 so the Detail slider can reach the higher fidelity, keeping a snappy ~25k default. 11/11 importMesh unit tests pass; framework + hmsc-int compile clean via SHIP_RUN_PACKAGE=0 ship. IMPORTANT: this is a framework Zig change, so the running dev host must be restarted (rjit dev hmsc-int) to load the new ceiling — the TSX/TS changes hot-reload but the 64MB limit is compiled into the binary.
